# CONTEXT.md — ClaimFlow Domain Glossary

> This document is the single source of truth for the domain language. Contains only the definition of business concepts and no implementation details.
> Format: One `##` title per term, definition + boundaries + relationship to other terms.

---

## Receipt (receipt record)

**Definition**: A record generated by a "submit receipt" action initiated by a consumer through WhatsApp. One submission corresponds to one Receipt.

**boundary**:
- A Receipt corresponds to a receipt image (or a message containing an image) sent by the consumer
- Receipt includes fields such as `phone` (submitter’s mobile phone number), `name` (consumer’s name), `ic` (ID card number, can be null), `image_filename`, `status`, `submitted_at`, etc.
- `name` and `ic` may be null when the first Receipt is created, and will be filled back in after the subsequent consumer sends the IC/name (within the same Session)
- Receipt life cycle: `pending_review` → `approved` / `rejected`

**Relationship to other terms**:
- A Session can produce multiple Receipts (users can submit multiple times on the same day)
- The review action of Receipt occurs in the Admin background and is not within the Bot dialogue process.

---

## Session

**Definition**: An active conversation process between a consumer's mobile phone number and the Bot, starting from the first time the user sends a message and ending when the process is completed (or times out).

**boundary**:
- Session is uniquely identified by `phone` (primary key)
- Session has a `state` field, which represents the current state of the conversation state machine
- State machine: `WAITING_IC` → `WAITING_RECEIPT` → `DONE` (Bot passive mode: does not actively welcome, but still has state advancement logic after receiving the message)
- Session has `receipt_count` and `receipt_count_date` for daily submission limit
- After the Session times out or is completed, a new Session will be created next time the user sends a message.
- In the same Session, after the consumer sends the IC/name, the system will backtrack and fill in the Receipt of `ic=null`/`name=null` in this Session.

**Relationship to other terms**:
- Session holds the current user's `ic` and `name`, which are associated with all Receipts submitted within the Session.
- Session is a Bot-side concept, and the Admin background does not directly operate Session.

---

## Campaign/Activity

**Definition**: A promotion campaign initiated by the brand (such as "Samsung June Promotion"), which is a business container for consumers to participate in receipt submission.

**boundary**:
- One Campaign = One Brand (1:1 relationship)
- A Campaign has rules: brand (brand), minimum amount (min_amount, fixed MYR), valid time window (start_date, end_date), whether to activate (is_active)
- Campaign fields are fixed: `id, brand, start_date, end_date, min_amount, is_active` (`brand` is free text, no default list)
- **Association between Receipt and Campaign**: When writing Receipt, the system queries the `campaigns` table, finds the Campaign with `start_date <= NOW() <= end_date` and `is_active=1`, takes the first one, and writes `campaign_id` into the Receipt record (**determined when writing, not changed later**)
- When there is no active Campaign, the Receipt is saved as usual (`campaign_id = NULL`), and the Bot does not send any message to the consumer.
- There is only one active Campaign at the same time (time does not overlap); different Campaigns are separated by different WhatsApp numbers
- Campaign can be edited, added, and deleted (Super Admin background CRUD management)
- Campaign configuration is stored in the database (`campaigns` table), and `config.yaml` is no longer used for static configuration.
- Campaign is highly customized - the fields are filled in according to specific customer needs and do not pursue generalization.

**Relationship to other terms**:
- A Deployment corresponds to a WhatsApp number and a Campaign
- The Receipt table has a `campaign_id` field (foreign key associated campaigns.id)
- Campaign's rules (brand, min_amount, etc.) determine whether the Receipt is valid

---

## Brand

**Definition**: The brand associated with the event (such as Samsung, Philips), the merchant brand on the Receipt needs to match the brand whitelist of the event.

**boundary**:
- Brand is an attribute of Campaign (one Campaign and one Brand)
- Brand whitelist is used to verify whether merchants on Receipt belong to the brand

---

## Admin (administration background)

**Definition**: An internal web interface used by operations staff to review Receipts, manage users, manage Campaigns, and view WhatsApp connection status.

**boundary**:
- Path prefix `/admin`
- Requires login (username/password), session authentication is required
- **Permission Level**:
  - **Super Admin**: Can operate all functions (review Receipt, manage Campaign, manage AdminUser, configure message template)
  - **Ordinary Admin**: Can only review Receipt (view list + approve/reject + send message manually), can see the current Campaign information (read-only) and Reject template content (cannot edit)
- After an ordinary Admin logs in, the current Campaign name + validity period is displayed at the top of the background, and there is also a "Campaign Information" page to view details (read-only)
- Multiple Campaign switching: There is a Campaign switching drop-down menu at the top of the background. Whichever Campaign you select will display the Receipt list of that one.
- Core operations: View Receipt list, AI recognition, manual review (approve/reject), manually send WhatsApp messages to consumers, export Excel, manage Campaign (Super Admin), manage AdminUser (Super Admin), configure message templates (Super Admin)

**Relationship to other terms**:
- The objects of Admin operation are Receipt (audit), AdminUser (user management), Campaign (activity management), MessageTemplate (message template)
- Admin does not directly operate Session (Session is a Bot-side concept)

---

## AdminUser (backend administrator)

**Definition**: A personnel account that has the right to log in to the Admin backend.

**boundary**:
- Stored in `admin_users` table, fields: `username` (PK), `password_hash`, `created_at`, `is_super_admin` (boolean, default false)
- The first registered AdminUser defaults to Super Admin (`is_super_admin = 1`)
- Passwords are stored using scrypt hashes
- **Permission Level**:
  - **Super Admin** (`is_super_admin = 1`): Can operate all functions (audit Receipt, manage Campaign, manage AdminUser, configure message template)
  - **Ordinary Admin** (`is_super_admin = 0`): can only review Receipt (view list + approve/reject + send message manually), can see the current Campaign information and Reject template content (read-only, cannot edit)
- It has no connection with the "consumer" on the business side (the consumer does not have an AdminUser account)

**Relationship to other terms**:
- AdminUser is the login subject of the Admin background
- Super Admin can manage Campaign and MessageTemplate
- Not directly related to Receipt/Consumer

---

## Consumer

**Definition**: An individual submitting a receipt via WhatsApp, uniquely identified by mobile number (`phone`).

**boundary**:
- The mobile phone number is the unique identifier of the Consumer, and the situation of the same person changing numbers is not considered (not processed in business)
- Consumer is not an independent table - Consumer information is scattered in `receipts` (submission records) and `sessions` (conversation status), and is related through `phone`
- The Admin background can view all Receipts of the consumer by mobile phone number.

**Relationship to other terms**:
- A Consumer can have multiple Sessions (conversation processes in different time periods)
- A Consumer can have multiple Receipts (multiple submissions)
- A Consumer's Receipt can belong to different campaigns (participate in different activities at different times)

---

## IC / ID number

**Definition**: Malaysian Identity Card number, in the format of `XXXXXX-XX-XXXX` (12 digits, separated by hyphens).

**boundary**:
- Consumers register by sending an IC image or text in a Bot conversation
- The IC is parsed and stored in the Session, and all Receipts associated with `ic=null` in the Session are traced back.
- When the IC is displayed in the Admin background, it will be desensitized to `XXXXXX-XX-****` (Phase 5 requirement)

---

## AI Recognition

**Definition**: The behavior automatically triggered by the Bot after the Receipt is submitted - calling OpenAI Responses API with GPT-5.6 Luna on the Receipt image and returning four structured fields: amount, brand, summary, and confidence.

**boundary**:
- Bot automatically calls AI recognition after the consumer submits the receipt image (no need for Admin to trigger manually)
- The recognition results are stored in the `ai_result` field of Receipt.
- v1 only supports `amount`, `brand`, `summary`, and `confidence`. Date, merchant, order number, and W1-W4 warning detection are explicitly out of scope.
- If extraction fails, Admin can retry it or manually verify the receipt before rejecting it. Approval remains disabled until extraction completes.
- AI recognition is an auxiliary means, and the final review decision rests with the manual operation of the Admin
- Admin can correct `amount` and `brand` before review. `summary` and `confidence` are read-only advisory output.

---

## Review

**Definition**: Admin user’s manual review action on Receipt, the result is `approved` or `rejected`.

**boundary**:
- Approve: Receipt status changes to `approved`, **the system does not automatically send messages** to consumers (Admin can send messages manually)
- Reject: The Receipt status changes to `rejected`, **the system does not automatically send the message**, and the Admin needs to manually click to send (using the default Reject template)
- After review, the Receipt status cannot be changed (current implementation)
- **Bot must not automatically send messages to consumers** - all messages sent to consumers must be manually clicked to send by the Admin

---

## Export

**Definition**: The operation of Admin user to export Receipt data to Excel file.

**boundary**:
- The export format is `.xlsx`, which contains the key fields of Receipt (including IC plain text, business needs)
- The export operation itself does not modify the Receipt status

---

## WhatsApp Client (WhatsApp client)

**Definition**: A WhatsApp connection established through the `whatsapp-web.js` library for receiving consumer messages.

**boundary**:
- **Multi-Client Architecture**: One Node.js process supports multiple WhatsApp Clients online at the same time (one Client for each Campaign)
- Each Client uses an independent `clientId` (LocalAuth support), and the session file exists in `.wwebjs_auth/session-<clientId>/`
- Connection status is stored by Campaign
- The QR code is displayed independently by Campaign (URL with `campaign_id` parameter)
- Bot **must not automatically send messages to consumers** - all messages sent to consumers must be manually clicked to send by the Admin
- Using unofficial WhatsApp Web protocol, there is a risk of account ban (noted in plan.md A.5)
- Run 1-2 Clients at the same time (small scale, enough memory)

---

## Deployment (deployment instance)

**Definition**: A stand-alone ClaimFlow system that supports multiple WhatsApp numbers, multiple campaigns, and multi-tenant data isolation.

**boundary**:
- One set of code and one Node.js process, supporting multiple WhatsApp Clients online at the same time (one Client for each Campaign)
- Different campaigns are distinguished by different WhatsApp numbers (consumers will participate in whichever account they add)
- Data segregated by Campaign (`receipts.campaign_id` related to `campaigns.id`)
- There is only one active Campaign at the same time (time does not overlap)

---

## Message Template

**Definition**: Default template configured by Admin for sending WhatsApp messages to consumers. Each Campaign can have its own template.

**boundary**:
- Templates are configured by Admin in the background and can be edited and used repeatedly.
- Templates are associated with Campaigns (different Campaigns can have different templates)
- Currently confirmed template type: **Reject template** (Admin manually chooses to send when reviewing rejection)
- Approve does not send a message (no template required)
- After receiving the Receipt, the Bot does not send a confirmation message (no template is required)
- All messages sent to consumers must be manually clicked to send by the Admin, and the Bot cannot send them automatically.

---

## Receipt Modification (receipt modification record)

**Definition**: After the Admin manually edits the Receipt field, the system automatically records the modification history.

**boundary**:
- Stored in the `receipt_modifications` table, fields: `id, receipt_id, modified_at, modified_by, field_name, old_value, new_value`
- The modification history is displayed in the expansion panel (`buildExpandPanel`) of the Receipt list page
- M6 (`note` field) is not required. Admin does not need to fill in the reason for modification.

---

## To be confirmed / to be designed

- **Mixed image and text processing solution**——Currently `messageHandler.js` cannot handle mixed image and text (the same message contains images + text), and IC text will be ignored. Phase 5-6 needs to be repaired, but the specific repair plan (how to change the routing logic) has not yet been designed.
- **Reject message template editing interface** - The template is pure fixed text (variables are not supported). Super Admin adds/edit/delete Reject templates on the Campaign management page. The specific UI design has not yet been confirmed.
- **Startup sequence of multiple WhatsApp Client architecture** - Will multiple Clients being initialized at the same time affect each other (Chromium resource competition)? Confirmation required.
- **Which Campaign can ordinary Admins see** - Which Campaign will ordinary Admins see by default after logging in? Is the allocation fixed, or can I see all campaigns (read-only)? Not confirmed yet.
